subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes + context-length profiling for Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme.ai>, Tom Mendes <tom.mendes@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0000
Subject: Pricing follow-up: token volumes + context-length profiling for Acme AI

Hi Sara / Tom —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few asks so we can produce an accurate pricing and capacity recommendation: 

Summary of notes from call:
- Primary use case: multi-turn customer support + knowledge-grounded generation for enterprise customers (200k MAU target in year 1).
- Key requirements: low-latency responses for chat flows (typical SLA 300–600ms), ability to handle longer context in support escalations (search + 1–2 docs).
- Deployment preference: start on Hosted for quick onboarding, evaluate Dedicated if predictable throughput is required.

To build a pricing estimate we need three pieces of profiling data from your side (or we can run a short profiling job):
1) Avg prompt tokens per request (prompt + system + few-shot context)
2) Avg completion tokens per request (typical answer length)
3) Proportion of sessions that require extended context (8k vs 32k vs 128k) — ballpark percentages are fine.

Target commercial inputs:
- Do you have a monthly budget range for model inference? (ballpark $/month)
- Is there a target unit economics metric you care about (e.g., $ per 1M tokens processed)?

If you can reply with the three profiling numbers above we’ll return:
- a hosted pricing pro forma (tokens/month -> $/month) with unit economics at $/1M tokens,
- a Dedicated capacity sizing estimate and committed cost if that looks attractive,
- suggestions for batching/caching and recommended context-length tier (8k/32k/128k) based on your distribution.

Attached: acme_context_profile_request.pdf — short template for the profiling numbers and example payloads. Also I attached a quick pricing workbook for reference.

Next steps: if you’d rather we run a 24-hour profiling run against a small sample, I can schedule it — we’ll need authorization and a sample of 500-1k requests (anonymized).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sara Patel <sara@acme.ai>

Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes + context-length profiling for Acme AI

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — good recap. Here are the numbers we can share now (rough averages from our staging logs):
- Avg prompt tokens: ~1,150 tokens (system + user + retrieval snippets; median ~900).
- Avg completion tokens: ~820 tokens (most replies are 300–1,200 tokens; long-form escalations up to ~6k seen ~1% of the time).
- Context-length distribution (estimates): 8k: 85%, 32k: 14%, 128k: 1%. The 128k use is for rare legal document summaries.

Budget: we’re targeting an initial monthly spend of $40k–$60k for inference, with a roadmap to $120k+/month in Yr1 if adoption scales. Our internal target unit economics is roughly $30 per 1M tokens as an upper bound; lower is obviously better.

Questions for you:
- How do you price long-tail 128k requests vs standard 8k/32k? Is there an easy way to cap spend on those?
- How much cost reduction can we expect from prefix/KV caching and batching for typical chat flows?

We can approve a profiling run — send details and we’ll provide 1,000 anonymized requests.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product, Acme AI
sara@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme.ai>, Tom Mendes <tom.mendes@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 16:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: token volumes + context-length profiling for Acme AI

Sara — really helpful, thanks for the detail. Initial read and high-level pricing guidance below. I’ll attach a quick pro forma in the workbook and we can refine after the profiling run.

Quick unit-economics sketch (hosted):
- Baseline assumptions (using your averages): avg request tokens = prompt (1,150) + completion (820) = ~1,970 tokens per request.
- At your target of 200k MAU with 0.75 requests/user/day -> ~150k requests/day -> ~295M tokens/day -> ~8.85B tokens/month.
- If we price at $25 / 1M tokens (target you mentioned lower bound), monthly inference cost ~= $221,250. At $30 / 1M tokens ~= $265,500/month.

Notes and levers to reduce cost:
- Caching (prefix / KV): for chat flows with repeated context we often see 15–40% token-level reduction depending on query similarity. If Acme can leverage document-level retrieval + heavy KV caching for short responses, expect ~20% reduction in total tokens.
- Batching: for peak throughput batching can improve throughput but may add 50–150ms latency depending on SLO — useful for non-interactive or slightly lenient latency windows.
- Quantization & model variant: using 8-bit quantized variants can reduce inference cost 20–30% vs fp16 depending on model and perf tradeoffs. We’ll recommend specific model/quantization combos after the profiling run.

Long-context pricing:
- 8k vs 32k vs 128k: our hosted pricing differentiates by context-length tier (8k base, 32k premium, 128k high-cost). 128k requests are billed at a higher per-token compute multiplier due to memory and compute overheads; rarer spikes imply we can offer consumption controls (quota, throttles, or pre-signed high-context tokens) to cap spend.
- Practically, for your distribution (85/14/1): most consumption will be at 8k/32k prices; 128k will only be a small fraction of tokens but can drive peak GPU memory needs on Dedicated.

Estimated hosted pro forma (very rough):
- Using your avg = 1,970 tokens/request and 150k req/day -> 8.85B tokens/month.
  - $25/1M -> $221,250/mo
  - $30/1M -> $265,500/mo
- With 20% caching savings -> 7.08B tokens/mo -> $177k–$212k/mo at $25–$30/1M.

Suggested next steps:
1) Let us run a 24–48 hour profiling job against 1,000 anonymized requests (your offer) — we’ll return precise prompt/completion distributions and model recommendations.
2) We’ll produce a Hosted pro forma and a Dedicated sizing + committed pricing (12-mo) to compare.
3) Put basic spend guardrails on 128k requests (quota + alerts) — we can help configure.

Jordan and Rishi are copied to help size Dedicated and pull the pricing workbook together. If that plan sounds good I’ll schedule the profiling run (needs a signed profiling NDA — DocuSign link below) and a 30-min follow to review results next week.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/samples/ACME-PROFILING-NDA
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACME-527

Thanks —
Marissa
